title: IdP Compatibility Playbook for SAML/SSO (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Create a practical, IdP-specific compatibility playbook and reference for Redwood's SAML/SSO integrations. This ticket captures: 1) canonical mapping patterns from common IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping) into RBAC v2 concepts (roles, grants, resource scopes); 2) audit logging and retention guidance for SAML assertions and mapping events; 3) IdP-specific test cases and edge-case handling (group overages, NameID formats, SP vs IdP initiated flows); 4) sample SAML attribute mappings and recommended IdP admin UI screenshots (links below); 5) migration guidance for customers upgrading from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with minimal disruption. Deliverables: a single playbook doc in Confluence + an internal runbook for on-call to debug SSO mismatches + a compatibility matrix maintained in the repo.

This should be authoritative for Solutions Engineering and Support when onboarding enterprise customers and for Product to codify expected behavior in the Console and API docs.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published with an IdP compatibility matrix that lists required IdP settings, attribute names, and known caveats for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping.
Examples for mapping at least three RBAC v2 role assignment patterns (role claim, groups-to-roles mapping, SCIM-based role provisioning) for each IdP.
Audit-logging proposal validated: what parts of the SAML assertion we persist, redaction rules, storage location, and retention policy (aligned with security & legal).
Test matrix + reproducible test cases checked in under security/rbac/idp-tests with automated smoke tests for SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows.
Mark doc as 'security-reviewed' and attach reviewer sign-off in the doc comments.
technical_notes: Okta: recommend two supported patterns - (A) SAML attribute 'roles' (multi-valued) set to application-specific values like 'redwood:admin' and (B) Groups claim mapped to SAML attribute 'groups'. For large group counts prefer Group Push (SCIM) or API-enrichment because group SAML claims are truncated. Use Okta's 'Include in SAML assertion' setting on group assignments.

Azure AD: must handle group overage. Azure will return _claim_names/_claim_sources with a link to MS Graph when >200 groups. Implement Graph enrichment flow: if assertion contains _claim_names, use the token in _claim_sources to fetch group list server-side, then perform mapping. Document required permissions: Directory.Read.All (application) and guidance on tenant admin consent.

Google Workspace: by default, group membership is not sent in SAML assertions. Document two options: configure a custom SAML attribute that pulls 'groups' for the user, or provision groups/roles via SCIM. Note: Google may send 'MemberOf' only when the admin configures it explicitly. Provide precise admin UI steps in playbook.

Ping: common deployments use PingFederate; Ping frequently requires explicit attribute contract configuration. Recommend using persistent NameID (Format=persistent) and an attribute named 'roles' or 'entitlements' that lists resource-level grants. Document handshake for signed assertions and assertion encryption settings we support (RSA-OAEP + AES256-GCM).

SAML Basics: Always validate Audience (SP EntityID) and Recipient (ACS URL). Support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows but require RelayState for IdP-initiated flow validation in our Console to map to the correct org/session. Store SAML Assertion fingerprint in audit log (sha256 hex) and the original Base64 assertion in secure blob storage for 30 days, redacting sensitive NameID/email when retention policy requires.
sample_mappings: Pattern A - Explicit role claim: IdP SAML attribute 'roles' -> 'redwood_role'. Expected values: 'redwood:admin', 'redwood:engineer', 'redwood:viewer'. This directly maps to RBAC v2 role objects during login.

Pattern B - Groups-to-roles mapping (common): IdP sends 'groups' attribute with group display names or IDs. Redwood mapping engine matches group strings to role bindings (configured per-org in Console). Example Okta group 'Redwood - Admins' -> maps to 'redwood:admin'.

Pattern C - SCIM provisioning for deterministic state: use SCIM v2 to provision Redwood role assignments directly. SCIM path /Groups or custom 'roles' extension maps to RBAC binding. Recommend for large enterprise customers wanting push-sync semantics.

Azure specific snippet: if assertion contains '_claim_names': { 'groups': 'src1' } then call Graph at src1.href with client credential to retrieve group ids. Fallback: if Graph unavailable, fall back to SCIM or deny role assignment and surface clear error in Console: 'group_overage_unresolved'.
migration_plan: Phase 1 - Documentation rollout: publish playbook and compatibility matrix; notify Solutions and Support channels.
Phase 2 - Soft enforcement: Console accepts both RBAC v1 and v2 mappings for 8 weeks. Nightly telemetry flagged for mismatches between SAML-provided attributes and RBAC v2 expectations.
Phase 3 - Migration tooling: provide a CLI that audits an org's current SAML config, suggests mapping rules, and optionally applies mappings (preview mode first).

Phase 4 - Cutover: after customer review, flip 'enforce_rbac_v2' flag with 14-day rollback. Provide a fallback 'edgemode' where requests are serviced with compatible legacy semantics for read-only operations for 30 days.
Rollback: document steps to revert to RBAC v1 mappings and where to clear cached SAML enrichment tokens.
test_plan: Unit tests: attribute mapping logic for 'roles' (single/multi-valued), 'groups' multi-valued, and nameid mapping; simulate Graph enrichment tokens for Azure.

Integration tests: end-to-end SP-initiated login and IdP-initiated login against test tenants for Okta, Azure, Google, Ping. Use vendor-provided test orgs and simulate >200 group cardinality for Azure.
Manual QA: Solutions Engineer to run the onboarding checklist for at least 3 enterprise customers (one per IdP except Ping) and record outcomes in playbook.
On-call playbook tests: simulate assertion parsing failures, signature validation errors, and Graph enrichment timeouts. Verify audit events are emitted with correct severity and content.
